structural_context: SITE Centers (SITC) completed a tax-free spin-off of Curbline Properties Corp. (CURB) on Oct 1, 2024 — transferred 79 convenience retail properties + $800M unrestricted cash to Curbline. Remaining SITC is a residual 'value-realization' open-air retail REIT (33 shopping centers, 22 wholly-owned + 11 JV), operating with one-for-four reverse stock split (Aug 2024), no revolver, simplified debt stack ($306.8M consolidated), and an explicit strategy to monetize the residual portfolio. CEO Lukes is simultaneously CEO of SITC and CURB. Forward return 2025-05-15 to ~one year out: -57.5%.

scores.claim_text: Management states the Company 'intends to realize value through operations and to consider various factors, including market conditions and differences between the public and private valuations of its portfolio, in evaluating whether and when to pursue additional asset sales. As of February 28, 2025, the Company was in the beginning stages of marketing a select number of assets for sale, though no assurances can be given that such efforts will result in additional asset sales.'
supports: filing_self_disclosure: 10-K signed 2025-02-28, ~5 months after Curbline spin (Oct 1, 2024)
From July 1, 2023 to Dec 31, 2024 generated $3.1B gross disposition proceeds (front-loaded into pre-spin / capitalizing Curbline period)
Capitalization at 12/31/2024: $306.8M debt + $801.7M market equity = $1.108B total cap; only 22 wholly-owned + 11 JV centers remaining
Mortgage Facility (Sep 2026 maturity, 13 properties as collateral) requires 115% of allocated loan amount on property releases — friction tax on dispositions
scores.M_check: Per priority 1 (stated plan vs disclosed pace) and Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational stage gap). Five months post-spin and 9 months post commencing the new wind-down strategy, the company is only 'in the beginning stages of marketing a select number of assets.' This is materially slower than the pre-spin pace (which moved $3.1B in 18 months) and the language degrades from 'plan' to 'consider whether and when' with the explicit dual exit excuse ('public vs private valuation differences'). The 115% release premium on Mortgage Facility properties is an internal friction that the filing does not quantify but which compounds dispositions math. Heuristic 8 (insider-pulse): execution is decelerating just as carrying costs (7.1% on $206.9M Mortgage Facility, $32.9M obligation to complete CURB redevelopments) accelerate.

M_value.post_spin_marketing_stage: beginning stages of marketing a select number of assets

scores.interpretation: Classic stage softening — pre-spin SITC narrated as 'disposing aggressively'; post-spin SITC narrates as 'considering whether and when.' This is a MODE not a RED because the company is still legally a going concern and continues to operate, but the gap between (a) the equity-market thesis of 'fast wind-down realizes per-share NAV' and (b) the actual disclosed pace ('beginning stages of marketing a select number') is the central source of the disappointment that materializes in the forward return. Heuristic for retail REIT wind-downs: when sale execution slows and the buyer is forced to live with carrying costs, holding-period NAV claims compress quickly.

scores.claim_text: The Company declared aggregate cash dividends of $1.04 per common share in 2024 (split-adjusted) — consisting of $0.52/share for Q1 2024 + $0.52/share for Q2 2024 — with NO regular quarterly cash dividends declared in Q3 or Q4 2024 (only the $44.58/share Curbline stock distribution). 'The decision to declare and pay future dividends... will be... influenced by operations and asset sales' subject to mortgage covenants on liquidity / net worth and the 90% REIT distribution requirement.
supports: Filing explicitly itemizes: 'The aggregate cash dividends declared in 2024 represent $0.52 per common share for each of the first and second quarters prior to the completion of the spin-off of Curbline'
By contrast, 2023 had $2.72/share including $0.64 special (paid Jan 2024); 2022 had $2.08/share — both regular quarterly cadence

Filing claims the company 'satisfied its REIT requirement of distributing at least 90% of ordinary taxable income with declared common and preferred share cash dividends of $64.4 million in 2024' — this is technically correct because the $44.58/share Curbline STOCK distribution counts for REIT 90% test
Filing concedes: 'The Company expects that its future dividend policy will be influenced by operations and asset sales' (no committed regular quarterly cadence post-spin)
scores.M_check: Per priority 2 (dividend cut + cap-allocation logic match) and Heuristic 7-equivalent for income claims. The filing is technically truthful — the special stock distribution of Curbline shares satisfied the 90% REIT requirement. BUT the equity story (retail REIT yielding cash quarterly) was effectively SUSPENDED in Q3-2024 without using the word 'suspended.' This is the structural-disclosure form of a dividend cut — the residual SITC went from a $0.52/qtr ($2.08/yr) run rate to ZERO regular cash dividend, with all future distributions tied to asset-sale proceeds. The framework should treat 'switched from regular cash to event-driven distributions' as a dividend cut for honesty-alpha purposes, especially when the language ('influenced by operations and asset sales') implies but does not name the cut. Magnitude: pre-spin cash yield ~$2.08/yr on a $61.16 split-adjusted Aug-2024 price ≈ 3.4% yield → post-spin: zero regular cash, only future event-driven.
scores.interpretation: SEV underdelivery on the dividend-disclosure-discipline axis. Filing accurately reports the cash-dividend amounts but does NOT label the change as a cut/suspension/pause. The pivot from a 100-quarter regular dividend cadence to an event-driven distribution model is the single most important fact about the post-spin equity story, and the filing's framing ('future dividends... influenced by operations and asset sales') buries it in conditional language. For honesty-alpha framework purposes, SITC is exhibiting the disclosure pattern of 'truthful in the numbers, evasive in the narrative.' The forward -57.5% return is consistent with the market correctly re-pricing a 3.4% yielder to a zero-yield wind-down vehicle once the absence of regular dividends becomes manifest through 2025.

scores.claim_text: The Company has $306.8M aggregate consolidated indebtedness consisting of (i) the $206.9M Mortgage Facility (Sept 2026 maturity, 2 one-year extension options, SOFR+275 with 3.5% floor = 7.1% at 12/31/24) secured by 13 properties, and (ii) the $99.9M Nassau Park Pavilion mortgage (Nov 2028 maturity, 6.7% fixed). The unconsolidated JVs have $441.8M total debt ($106.6M at SITC's share) at 6.2% weighted-average rate / 3.6-year weighted-average maturity. No revolving credit facility (terminated August 2024).
supports: Filing self-discloses: 'In preparation for the spin-off of Curbline Properties, the Company repaid all of its unsecured indebtedness and terminated its revolving credit facility in August 2024. As a result, the Company does not maintain a line of credit that can be used to fund working capital needs.'
Mortgage Facility floor of 3.5% on SOFR exposes upside-only rate risk (no benefit from rate cuts unless SOFR > 3.5%)
SITC's share of JV debt ($106.6M) at 6.2% WAR with 3.6yr WAM means meaningful refinance risk concentrated 2027-2028
Combined consolidated + look-through JV debt: $306.8M + $106.6M = $413.4M against $801.7M market cap = ~52% LTV at market
scores.M_check: Per priority 4 (debt maturity ladder). The maturity ladder discloses honestly: $206.9M due Sept 2026, $99.9M due Nov 2028, JV $106.6M weighted ~3.6 years. The MODE concern is the structural combination: (a) no revolver = forced reliance on cash on hand and disposition proceeds for any liquidity need; (b) the 3.5% SOFR floor means the 7.1% all-in rate on the largest tranche won't reset down if rates fall; (c) the 115% release premium creates a per-property tax on dispositions that compounds with the 7.1% carry on the residual balance — i.e., the disposition machine is self-bleeding. Heuristic 3 stage-gap: the filing's narrative is 'simplified debt structure' / 'prudent leverage levels' but the post-spin reality is that EVERY balance-sheet flexibility lever (unsecured market access, revolver, preferred stock) was paid off / terminated as a condition of the spin, leaving SITC structurally rigid.
scores.interpretation: Debt-disclosure itself is PASS-quality on the numbers; MODE rating reflects the implication-gap. The 'simplified debt structure' framing understates the structural rigidity (no revolver, floor rate on senior tranche, release premium friction). For wind-down REIT analysis, the Sept-2026 maturity is the binding constraint: SITC needs to either (a) execute material dispositions before then, (b) extend (2 one-year options exist), or (c) refi at then-prevailing rates. The two-year extension options provide a meaningful safety margin, which is why this is MODE not SEV.

scores.claim_text: Capitalization at December 31, 2024 was $306.8M of debt and $801.7M of market equity (calculated as common shares outstanding multiplied by $15.29, the closing price on the NYSE at December 31, 2024). The Company recorded $66.6M of impairment charges in FY2024 'triggered by changes in hold period assumptions.'
supports: Balance sheet: Additional paid-in capital $3,981.6M; Accumulated distributions in excess of net income $(3,473.5M); net = $508.1M book equity (before noncontrolling)
Pre-spin paid-in capital was $5,990.9M (per balance sheet) — $2.0B was reclassified out as part of the Curbline spin distribution

Filing acknowledges 'differences between the public and private valuations of its portfolio' as a strategic factor (i.e., management knows the stock is trading below their internal NAV but does not say by how much)
$66.6M impairment in 2024 was 'triggered by changes in hold period assumptions' — i.e., admission that the marked carrying values were not realizable at prior planned holding periods
scores.M_check: Per priority 5 (NAV claims vs market price). The disclosure acknowledges the public-private valuation discount EXISTS (oblique reference) without quantifying it. Critical 2-mode read: Mode A — the explicit claim that there is a public/private gap is verified by the company's own observation. Mode B — the IMPLIED claim is that the wind-down will close the gap; the $66.6M impairment in 2024 is an admission that even the BOOK carrying values had to come down when hold periods shortened. Heuristic 3 + Heuristic 8: when management writes down assets specifically because they reduced holding periods, that is the FILING WRITING DOWN ITS OWN NAV CLAIM PROSPECTIVELY. The forward path mathematically requires either (a) sale prices materially above marked carrying values, or (b) further write-downs as hold periods compress further. The $15.29 closing price vs the implied 'private valuation' framing is the core 2025 thesis SITC was being marketed on, and the impairment is the first concrete signal that the gap may resolve in the WRONG direction.
scores.interpretation: SEV underdelivery on the NAV-discipline axis. The filing makes the qualitative claim that there is a public/private valuation gap (the thesis underpinning the equity), but the only quantitative evidence it provides moves in the OPPOSITE direction — a $66.6M hold-period-driven impairment. For a wind-down vehicle, the gap between asserted NAV and proven NAV is the entire investment case; SITC's filing acknowledges the gap exists but provides no quantification and provides counter-evidence in the impairment line. Forward -57.5% return is consistent with the market re-pricing toward (and through) the marked book equity rather than toward management's implied private-market NAV.

scores.claim_text: CEO David R. Lukes serves simultaneously as President/CEO/Director of BOTH SITE Centers and Curbline Properties (since September 2024). Under the Shared Services Agreement, the Curbline Operating Partnership pays SITC a monthly fee of 2.0% of Curbline's Gross Revenue, with a 3-year term and a $12.0M termination-for-convenience penalty on the second anniversary. Mr. Lukes and the CIO are not employed by SITC; the CFO, CAO and General Counsel are SITC-employed.
supports: Filing self-discloses: 'Mr. Lukes has also served as President, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Curbline Properties since September 2024'

Filing self-discloses: 'The Company is not a party to employment contracts with its Chief Executive Officer or Chief Investment Officer whose services are provided' [via the Shared Services Agreement / Curbline]
Shared Services Agreement: Curbline pays SITC 2.0% of Gross Revenue (i.e., the relationship is structured as Curbline paying SITC for shared mgmt rather than the reverse)
Termination-for-convenience penalty of $12.0M payable to SITC if Curbline exits at second anniversary
scores.M_check: Per priority 6 (insider behavior near spinoff distribution) and the framework's structural-conflict heuristic. This is the textbook dual-fiduciary problem: the CEO has equity / compensation exposure to BOTH the entity that received the high-quality assets and $800M of cash (Curbline) AND the entity that received the residual portfolio (SITC). Under standard agency theory, the CEO's wind-down execution at SITC may be slowed (or biased toward favorable deals for Curbline) by the conflict, and the structure makes accountability diffuse. The Shared Services payment direction (Curbline → SITC) is engineered to provide SITC with operating-cash optionality, but the deeper question is whether asset-allocation choices made in the YEAR BEFORE the spin (specifically: which assets went to Curbline, which stayed at SITC, and the $800M cash transfer) were optimized for the residual SITC shareholder. Heuristic for spinoff backtests: when the same CEO runs both sides, the residual entity often underperforms because the high-quality asset selection happens at the spin design phase and is locked in. Comparative outcomes — Curbline (CURB) post-spin vs SITC post-spin — would be the natural Mode B verification (not available within filing alone, but the structural ASYMMETRY is verifiable in the spin terms themselves).

M_value.sitc_kept_in_spin: 33 shopping centers (22 wholly-owned + 11 JV) + $530M mortgage facility + debt-redemption obligations

scores.interpretation: RED on structural-conflict grounds. The filing is fully transparent about the dual-CEO arrangement (which is its honesty-alpha credit) but the structure itself is the red flag — the SITC residual is left to wind down under a CEO whose primary equity exposure flips to Curbline (the better assets + $800M cash). For backtest honesty-alpha framework: the disclosure is honest, but the STRUCTURE places SITC shareholders in a position where best execution against their interest cannot be assumed. Combined with C1 (slow disposition pace post-spin) and C2 (dividend pause), the dual-CEO arrangement is the explanation. This is the cleanest forward-return predictive signal in the filing — a wind-down REIT whose accountable executive sits at the spin-co rather than the residual is structurally disposed to deliver weak residual-shareholder outcomes. -57.5% forward return is consistent.

scores.claim_text: The Company has only TWO unconsolidated joint ventures: (a) Dividend Trust Portfolio JV LP — 20.0% effective ownership, 10 operating properties, partner = 'Chinese Institutional Investors' — Company is obligated to maintain the REIT status of the JV's REIT subsidiary; failure could result in substantial liability to its partner; (b) RVIP IIIB, Deer Park, IL — 25.75% with Prudential, 1 property. Total investments-in-and-advances to unconsolidated JVs at 12/31/2024 = $30.4M.
supports: Filing self-discloses partner identities and percentages in the JV table
Dividend Trust Portfolio JV: 10 of SITC's 11 JV properties = 91% of JV exposure concentrated in a single 20%-owned vehicle with Chinese institutional partner

Filing flags: 'the Company is obligated to maintain the REIT status of the Dividend Trust Portfolio joint venture's REIT subsidiary and the Company's failure to do so could result in substantial liability to its partner'
JV-level $441.8M debt ($106.6M SITC share) with 3.6-year WAM means the 91%-concentrated DTP vehicle is also a debt-refinance concentration
scores.M_check: Per priority 7 (joint venture interest economics). The filing is forthcoming about the JV partner identities and the REIT-status indemnity, which is honesty-alpha credit. But the implied claims that warrant Mode B verification: (a) the 20% interest in DTP gives SITC only minority economic exposure and no operational control over 10 of its 11 JV properties — which means the disposition narrative ('we can monetize residual assets') applies to only 22 of 33 centers in any straightforward sense; (b) the Chinese institutional partner is an inherent geopolitical-process risk (CFIUS-adjacent dynamics on US commercial real estate, especially with elevated US-China tensions post-2024 election) that is NOT disclosed in the filing's risk factors; (c) the REIT-status indemnity creates an asymmetric tail liability for SITC if any technical violation occurs. Heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure): a Chinese institutional partner in a US REIT joint venture is not an SEC filer, so the M-source counterparty check is structurally blocked.
scores.interpretation: MODE underdelivery on the JV-economics axis. The disclosures are honest on identity and structure but the IMPLIED claim that the JV portfolio is monetizable on the same timeline as the wholly-owned portfolio is unsupported — minority interests in single-partner JVs (especially with foreign institutional partners) typically require buy-sell triggers, partner consent, or a coordinated liquidation that takes years. For wind-down REIT analysis: 11/33 = 33% of properties effectively delayed in the disposition timeline. Geopolitical-risk omission (Chinese partner under elevated US-China tensions) is a process noteworthy but not large enough alone to lift to SEV.

scores.claim_text: The Company recorded a write-off of $21.2M of fees related to the terminated Mortgage Commitment (the original $1.1B mortgage facility on 40 properties obtained in October 2023). The Company also recorded $66.6M of impairment charges in 2024 triggered by changes in hold-period assumptions, plus debt-extinguishment costs of $0.9M (Term Loan), $3.9M (RCF), $6.7M (Senior Notes), and $10.1M (property releases from Mortgage Facility).
supports: Filing self-discloses: 'For the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company wrote-off $21.2 million of fees relating to the Mortgage Commitment to Debt extinguishment costs'

Mortgage Commitment was for $1.1B secured by 40 properties (originally obtained October 2023) — the actual Mortgage Facility ended up as $530M secured by 23 properties (only 13 still encumbered at 12/31/24)
Impairment trigger 'changes in hold period assumptions' is an explicit admission that prior accounting assumed longer hold periods than the new wind-down strategy implies
Aggregate one-time costs in 2024: $21.2M + $66.6M + $0.9M + $3.9M + $6.7M + $10.1M = ~$109M of friction
scores.M_check: Per priority 8 (claim evolution; 10-K narrative discipline). The $21.2M write-off discloses the magnitude of the cost of CHANGING THE PLAN — originally a $1.1B / 40-property facility (consistent with maintaining a larger wholly-owned portfolio long-term), redesigned to $530M / 23-property facility (consistent with shorter hold + disposition-driven strategy). This is the cleanest direct evidence in the filing that management's prior plan was abandoned and the cost of that abandonment was material ($21.2M is ~2.6% of market cap). The $66.6M impairment under 'hold period change' is the same disclosure dressed differently. Combined: the filing is honestly disclosing that the strategic pivot cost approximately $87.8M in non-cash + one-time cash items, against $801.7M market cap = 11% of market cap value-destroyed in transition costs alone.
scores.interpretation: MODE — the disclosure is COMPLETE on the numbers; the framework's concern is the implicit cost of strategy churn. ~$109M of one-time friction in a single year, against an $801.7M market cap, is a material drag on wind-down NAV math that is buried in distinct line items. Heuristic 8 (insider pulse): the magnitude of these abandonment costs is direct evidence that the management team's prior plans (held through October 2023 financing commitment) did not anticipate the spin / wind-down path that was decided on in 2024. PASS on disclosure discipline; MODE on what the disclosure implies about planning quality.

scores.claim_text: XBRL fact 'sitc:PeriodForWhichCompanyMayNoLongerQualifyAsReit = P4Y' is reported in the filing (i.e., management has tagged a 4-year period during which the Company may no longer qualify as a REIT). The narrative discusses: 'The amount of non-qualifying assets and income the Company can own and earn while still maintaining its REIT status has decreased in recent years due to the reduction in the size of the Company's operations resulting from asset sales and the spin-off of Curbline and may continue to decrease. Accordingly, the Company's ability to qualify and remain qualified as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes is not certain and cannot be assured.'
supports: XBRL: ix:nonNumeric name='sitc:PeriodForWhichCompanyMayNoLongerQualifyAsReit' value='P4Y' — i.e., the Company has machine-tagged a 4-year de-REIT window
Narrative: 'amount of non-qualifying assets and income the Company can own and earn while still maintaining its REIT status has decreased in recent years... and may continue to decrease'
REIT requires distribution of >=90% of taxable income; failure means 4-year disqualification + corporate-tax treatment
Filing concedes: 'ability to qualify and remain qualified as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes is not certain and cannot be assured'
scores.M_check: Per Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational stage gap) and the framework's structural-disclosure escalation rule. A retail REIT discussing a possible loss of REIT status within a 4-year window is a material disclosure that has direct equity-value implications: (a) loss of REIT pass-through tax treatment would convert SITC to a regular C-corp paying ~21% federal corporate tax on operating income, materially compressing distributable cash flow; (b) the 4-year disqualification period is the maximum penalty under §856 et seq.; (c) the 'concentration in non-qualifying assets' framing implies that the residual SITC business has become structurally smaller than the qualifying-income test denominator. The XBRL tag P4Y is not boilerplate — most operating REITs do not tag this fact at all. SITC's choice to machine-tag a 4-year de-REIT window is the cleanest forward-looking adverse signal in the filing.

M_value.trigger_for_concern: spin-off + asset sales reduced qualifying-income denominator

scores.interpretation: SEV underdelivery — but specifically on the magnitude axis rather than the disclosure-discipline axis. The filing IS honest (this is honesty-alpha credit and a key reason this is SEV not RED) — it both tags the XBRL fact and includes the narrative disclosure. But for a backtest evaluating the equity story, the IMPLIED claim of the wind-down REIT thesis is 'we'll distribute cash to shareholders and dissolve' — and a 4-year de-REIT window means that if the disposition pace doesn't accelerate, the entity may need to convert to a non-REIT corporate vehicle during the wind-down itself, with adverse tax consequences. This is among the most underweighted forward-looking signals in the filing: when a REIT machine-tags a P4Y de-REIT period, that is management saying explicitly that the qualifying-income safety margin has thinned. Combined with C1 (slow disposition pace) and C2 (no regular cash dividend), this directly explains the forward -57.5% return.

summary: SITC FY2024 10-K: 8 R/f/M claims scored. Severity counts: PASS=0 MODE=4 SEV=3 RED=1 UNV=0. The filing is broadly HONEST on the numbers (this is honesty-alpha credit; nothing rises to fraud-signal territory in disclosure-discipline terms) but the AGGREGATE picture across the 8 claims is structurally bearish: (a) the disposition pace materially decelerated post-spin while the narrative softened to 'whether and when'; (b) the regular quarterly cash dividend was effectively suspended in Q3 2024 without using the word; (c) the $66.6M hold-period-driven impairment plus $21.2M Mortgage Commitment write-off plus $20.6M other extinguishment costs aggregate to ~$109M (~14% of market cap) of strategy-churn friction; (d) the CEO is dual-headed with Curbline (RED structural conflict); (e) 33% of properties (11/33) are in JVs concentrated 91% in a single 20%-owned vehicle with a Chinese institutional partner; (f) management machine-tagged a 4-year de-REIT period in XBRL. Forward -57.5% return is well-explained by the dividend-pause + slow-disposition-pace + management-conflict combination, all of which the filing discloses but does not headline. Honesty-alpha framework conclusion: the filing earns honesty credit on numerical disclosure but fails the implication-discipline test — the narrative consistently softens what the numbers and XBRL tags reveal. C5 (dual CEO conflict) is the structural RED that anchors the forward-return prediction.
framework_notes: Mode A (claim verification): the filing is consistently truthful on quantified facts (cash dividends, debt balances, JV partners, impairment magnitudes). No Mode-A REDs.

Mode B (implied-verification derivation): the central Mode-B finding is the gap between the wind-down REIT equity thesis ('fast disposition realizes per-share NAV') and the IMPLIED facts the filing discloses (slow post-spin pace, dividend pause, dual-CEO conflict, P4Y de-REIT XBRL tag). This Mode-B aggregation is what produces the -57.5% forward-return prediction.

Structural-conflict heuristic (new): for spin-offs where the SAME CEO runs both the spin-co (high-quality assets + cash transfer) and the residual (wind-down portfolio), the residual entity should be flagged RED on structural-conflict grounds even when individual numerical disclosures pass. SITC C5 is the prototype.

REIT-specific machine-tag heuristic: an XBRL fact 'PeriodForWhichCompanyMayNoLongerQualifyAsReit' with a non-null value (here P4Y) is an unusually strong forward-looking signal — most REITs do not file this tag. Worth a M-source connector to automatically flag any REIT that machine-tags this fact.

Dividend-suspension-disguised-as-policy heuristic: when a REIT transitions from regular quarterly cash dividends to 'event-driven distributions influenced by operations and asset sales' without using the words suspend/cut/reduce, the disclosure should be treated as a SEV underdelivery for honesty-alpha purposes. Most retail REIT analyst frameworks treat dividend cuts as PASS-discipline if the math reconciles, but the LANGUAGE choice is the load-bearing signal.
process_rules_discovered: M-source gap: SEC XBRL machine-tag scanner that flags any REIT issuer reporting a non-null 'PeriodForWhichCompanyMayNoLongerQualifyAsReit' would have caught this without text scanning.

M-source gap: spin-off dual-CEO detection (matching CEO across two related entities post-spin) requires linking director/officer rosters across the parent and the spin-co; currently only achievable by manually cross-referencing both 10-Ks.

M-source gap: post-spin disposition-velocity tracking requires comparing pre-spin trailing 12-month gross proceeds to post-spin trailing 6-month proceeds, which needs structured property-sale parsing across 8-Ks and 10-Qs.
Heuristic candidate: 'dividend cadence-change without dividend-cut vocabulary' as a stand-alone SEV-trigger for income-oriented securities (REITs, BDCs, MLPs, preferred-heavy issuers).
